title: The composite of differential operators of orders k and k' has order at most k + k'
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map from R to S and S-modules L, M, N, the composite of a differential operator D of order k with one D' of order k' is again a differential operator, of order at most k + k' (statement lines 34900-34906). The proof does not invoke a symbolic calculus or a filtration: it writes the commutator of D'D with multiplication by a function g, splits it by inserting D(gx) in the middle, and observes that the two resulting terms are compositions of operators of strictly smaller order, which sets up the induction on k + k' (proof lines 34908-34915). The splitting trick is the substance and the author displays it explicitly. H2.
